args.title: checkout-api: unhealthy deploy v2.3.1 rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the deploy of v2.3.1 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with error rate at ~18%.

Remediation: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. The first rollback attempt was a partial failure — the rollout halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all three regions.

Current state: all production regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%.

Follow-ups: Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet determined; no re-deploy of v2.3.1 should be attempted without investigation. The orchestrator error that caused the partial rollback should also be reviewed. Note v2.3.1-rc is also marked unhealthy in staging.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident (INC-0001) was in fact created despite the timeout — no retry needed.

## Summary

**Incident resolved: checkout-api rolled back to v2.3.0 in all production regions**

1. **Diagnosed** — checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three regions, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent production-healthy release (v2.3.1-rc is unhealthy in staging too).

2. **Rolled back** — the first rollback halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed fleet (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west/eu-west on unhealthy v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout.

3. **Verified** — all regions now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

4. **Incident opened** — INC-0001 (SEV2) documenting the failure, the partial-rollback complication, and follow-ups. The initial create call timed out client-side, but the incident did get created; I confirmed via list rather than retrying, to avoid a duplicate page.

Notes for follow-up: no policy approval was required here since v2.3.0 has a prior healthy production record — the approval gate applies only to versions that have never been healthy in production. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failures is still unknown, and the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollback is worth investigating; both are flagged in the incident.
